title: MemoryStore builds the filename from the elder's name and sanitises only spaces
method: input probe on elder_name with save/load round-trip
observed_at_discovery: safe_name = memory.elder_name.lower().replace(' ', '_'). With elder_name '../ESCAPED' and data_dir <tmp>/memory, save() wrote <tmp>/escaped.json -- one level above the store's own directory. The wizard sanitises its config filename correctly two files away (re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', ...)), and a previous audit checked that one and cleared it (FS-1e8f7a8ce112); the memory store never got the same treatment. Rated low because elder_name is caregiver-typed, not attacker-supplied. The realistic cost is a name with a slash in it splitting the memory to a path load() cannot find, so Cura meets her as a stranger every morning and nothing reports the loss. pytest exit 1, 2 failed of 6.
